newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Czech PX50 soars to year high led by utilities.
newsitem.headline: Czech PX50 soars to year high led by utilities.

text.p: The Czech PX50 index surged nearly two percent on Thursday to a year high of 591.3 as the two most heavily capitalised shares on the bourse, utilities SPT Telecom and CEZ, continued to soar.
CEZ gained 51 crowns, 4.4 percent, to 1,210 and SPT rose 169 crowns, 4.7 percent, to 3,744.
Despite the second day of solid gains from the two issues, dealers cautioned that low liquidity had played its part in pushing their prices higher.
"Volumes are very thin, when you come to the market looking for a bigger parcel of shares it doesn't take much interest (effort) to move the prices," said Jan Sykora of Wood & Company.
SPT and CEZ account for 34 percent of the PX50 index's total capitalisation and have, if they move together, a near decisive influence on the direction of the market.
The index's two biggest banking stocks both moved lower. Ceska Sporitelna lost two crowns to 330 and Komercni Banka fell six crowns to 2,494.
There was little noticible effect on prices of energy distributors despite the continuation of a nationwide rail strike into its third day.
